definition: Incipient means just beginning to exist or develop.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word incipient. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know incipient should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: An incipient smile tugged at the witness's mouth before she caught it and looked down.
Developing goes further than incipient: an incipient project has barely appeared, while a developing one is visibly under way.
Full-blown goes far beyond incipient — the storm has arrived in full force, with nothing 'just beginning' about it.

Budding means just beginning to grow, and it keeps the garden's hopefulness — budding careers, budding friendships. Incipient is the clinical cousin, neutral to wary: incipient rust, incipient panic. Both mark the earliest stage; budding cheers it on, incipient watches it warily.

Emerging means coming into view and gathering notice — an emerging trend is a stage past the very start, already showing its direction. Incipient sits earlier: the thing has only just crossed the line into existing, easy to miss altogether.

Walking the rows at dawn, the vineyard manager found incipient mildew on two leaves — a gray dust you'd miss from a meter away — and had the sprayer out before the dew burned off.
Incipient flags the very first stage of something that is developing — often something you'd rather stop.
Where inchoate (this unit) describes the shapelessness of what has begun, incipient simply marks how early it is: the thing has just crossed the line into existing.
Incipient is the clinician's and forecaster's word for a thing at its very first stage — incipient rust, incipient panic.
It is neutral about shape (that is inchoate's job, one card back) and slightly wary in tone: what is incipient often wants catching early.
